#!/bin/bash
# Flux batch script converted from Slurm

# NOTE: Run with: flux batch <this_script>

# Slurm resources:
#   --nodes=1
#   --cpus-per-task=16
#   --time=2:00:00
#   --mem=40GB
#   --gres=gpu:1
#   --job-name=se_fulldrop_good_ResNet4_num_blocks2x1x1x1_squeeze_and_excitation1_drop0
#   --output=se_fulldrop_good_ResNet4_num_blocks2x1x1x1_squeeze_and_excitation1_drop0.out

#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -c 16
#flux: --time-limit=2h
#flux: --job-name=se_fulldrop_good_ResNet4_num_blocks2x1x1x1_squeeze_and_excitation1_drop0
#flux: --output=se_fulldrop_good_ResNet4_num_blocks2x1x1x1_squeeze_and_excitation1_drop0.out

# Omitted Slurm option: --mem=40GB
# Flux memory requests are site/config dependent and not universally portable.
# Performance implication: job may be scheduled on a node with insufficient memory, risking OOM kills or degraded performance.

# Omitted Slurm option: --gres=gpu:1
# Flux GPU requests are site/config dependent (often via custom resource types).
# Performance implication: job may start without a GPU, causing failure or severe slowdown.

module load python/intel/3.8.6
module load openmpi/intel/4.0.5

source ../venvs/dl/bin/activate

time python3 main.py --config resnet_configs/se_fulldrop_good_ResNet4.yaml --resnet_architecture se_fulldrop_good_ResNet4_num_blocks2x1x1x1_squeeze_and_excitation1_drop0

reasons: The original Slurm job required 1 GPU (`--gres=gpu:1`) but the Flux resource section does not request any GPU resources; on GPU-managed systems this may allocate CPU-only resources and the job may fail or run much slower.

The original Slurm job requested 40GB of memory (`--mem=40GB`) but the Flux resource section has no memory request; on systems that schedule/enforce memory this may under-provision the job and risk OOM.
